title: Feedback confluence - action tiles & quick proposals (2024-11-13)
content:
Executive summary:

This note consolidates ~16 customer threads (enterprise + AI-native) from Oct-Nov 2024 into a compact set of "action tiles" — small, scoped engineering/product experiments that map to clear customer pain, expected impact, and a low-friction owner. Purpose: create a 2-week probe plan we can run with SRE + Serve runtime team to capture quick wins and clear go/no-go signals for larger items (Dedicated/reserved capacity, Private rollout work).

Why this is different:
- Focused on tiny, testable changes (tiles) rather than full feature specs.
- Prioritizes cost/latency trade-offs customers actually measure in production, not just feature wishlists.
- Packs customer quotes and a suggested measurement plan for each tile.

Synthesis headline signals (pattern-level):
1) Latency tail matters for multi-step flows: several customers reported 95th percentile spikes when KV cache miss rates increased for multi-turn chat.
2) Cost transparency + mitigation: product teams want clearer per-route token cost attribution and a light auto-quantization suggestion for non-sensitive workloads.
3) Private networking friction: onboarding Private (VPC) often stalls on egress/NAT and KMS policies; customers ask for a concise checklist and a staging template.
4) Fallback behavior needs policy knobs: customers want deterministic fallback by cost tier/model-similarity rather than opaque fallthrough.

Action tiles (prioritized low-friction probes):
- Tile A: "KV miss telemetry spike" (owner: SRE / serving-runtime)
  * What: instrument and emit a labelled metric for "kv_hit_rate_by_route" and a simple 95/99p latency slice when kv_hit_rate < 80%.
  * Why: Three enterprise customers have postmortems tying user-facing latency spikes to low prefix cache rates during scheduled jobs.
  * Success metric: Correlate kv_hit_rate < 80% incidents with latency delta >= 120ms in 95p within 48 hours of rollout.
  * Timebox: 7 days (instrument, dashboards, one customer pilot).

- Tile B: "Fallback policy preview endpoint" (owner: product-hosted-api + infra)
  * What: lightweight /v1/fallback-preview that returns the ordered list of fallback models/routes for a given route config (no inference).
  * Why: Customers currently test fallback behavior manually; predictable fallbacks reduce outages during capacity pressure.
  * Success metric: Two pilot customers confirm mapping and roll out a canary with fallback = true.
  * Timebox: 10 days (API, docs, 1 pilot).

- Tile C: "Cost-per-route micro-report" (owner: developer-experience)
  * What: per-route week-to-date token spend, avg token latency, and top 3 contributing prompt templates in a CSV export.
  * Why: Product teams request finer attribution before committing to Dedicated.
  * Success metric: 3 customers sign off that the CSV helped a budgeting decision.
  * Timebox: 5 days (query + export).

- Tile D: "Private onboarding staging template" (owner: solutions-engineering)
  * What: repo with terraform snippets, KMS policy templates, and a NAT/e2e checklist for common cloud providers.
  * Why: Onboarding stalls are the most frequent blocker for Private deals.
  * Success metric: Reduce customer onboarding time (initial setup -> first test inference) from median 14 days to <= 5 days for two pilots.
  * Timebox: 12 days (template + 1 onboarding run).

Customer vignettes (condensed):
1) Med-SaaS analytics company (mid-market): "We saw chat latency burst in long workflows; engineers traced it to cold KV cache after autoscale events. We need recommendations to keep tail small without blowing cost." (asks: kv caching visibility, pre-warm knobs on autoscale).
2) Large enterprise (regulated): "We can move to Private but KMS entitlements and egress governance are killing momentum — we need a concrete template and a 'safe-by-default' networking plan that our security team can sign off on." (asks: onboarding template, audit logs).
3) AI-native startup: "We want to try quantized variants for batched inference. If we can get a 'suggested quantization profile' per model for our workload, that'll cut cost and keep latency acceptable." (asks: optimize suggestions, perf guidance).

Synthesis -> quick product/engineering implications:
- Minimum telemetry: kv_hit_rate_by_route, fallback_preview_path, per-route cost CSV. These are high-value, low-effort and directly requested.
- Short-term UX: small API endpoints & CSV exports improve decision velocity for customers evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted.
- Commercial enablement: solutions-engineering templates for Private will increase conversion velocity on Legal/InfoSec gating items.

Proposed next steps (two-week probe plan):
1) Week 1: Implement Tile C (Cost CSV) + Tile A metrics instrumentation. Get dashboards live and run a smoke test with internal sandbox data. (Owners: DX + SRE)
2) Week 2: Ship fallback-preview endpoint + create the Private onboarding repo skeleton. Invite two pilot customers (one enterprise, one startup) to test. (Owners: product-hosted-api + solutions-eng)

Measurement & gating criteria:
- If Tile A uncovers > 3 recurring incidents reducible by pre-warm policy, escalate to serving-runtime to draft an autoscale pre-warm feature.
- If Tile D reduces onboarding median time to <= 5 days for >1 pilot, convert repo into a standard 'Private quickstart' offering.

Open questions & risks:
- Risk: Collecting per-route cost data may reveal internal pricing mismatches. Mitigation: start as CSV export behind a feature flag and notify acct managers before wide roll-out.
- Question: Do we have permission to surface model quantization suggestions automatically for customer data? Need legal sign-off for automated profiling.

Notes & quick links (for triage):
- Slack thread: #cs-runtime-ops thread-4672 — raw customer logs and sample traces.
- Jira: JIRA-3248 (feature request: per-route cost export)
- Confluence draft: /feedback-lab/kv-cache-friction (engineering notes, raw customer traces)

Appendix: raw quotes (redacted):
- "We had two hours of degraded chat because our cache wasn't primed after autoscale — users churned sessions." — enterprise support ticket #9876
- "If you send us a one-click template for VPC+KMS we can close the PO this quarter." — procurement email from regulated customer.

Quick owner checklist (to start):
- SRE: add kv_hit_rate_by_route + 95/99p latency tags (due: +7d)
- DX: build per-route CSV export and sample dashboard template (due: +5d)
- Product-hosted-api: implement fallback-preview endpoint (due: +10d)
- Solutions-eng: begin Private onboarding repo skeleton and coordinate pilot (due: +12d)

This doc is intentionally lightweight — aim is to move fast on measurable probes and capture whether these small fixes materially reduce onboarding friction and tail-latency incidents. Please add comments inline or ping in #cs-runtime-ops to prioritize pilots.

Last edited by: Aisha Romero (cs); next update: 2024-12-12 or after pilot results.
